title: What to Do If SASSA Asks You to Update Your Information (Step-by-Step)
description: Received an SMS, letter, or call asking you to update your information with SASSA? Follow this step-by-step guide to respond safely, keep your grant active, and avoid scams.

steps.title: Step 1: Verify the Request Is Genuine
steps.content:
Before doing anything, confirm the request is really from SASSA. Scammers frequently send fake SMS messages and make fake calls pretending to be SASSA.

**How to Identify a Genuine SASSA Review SMS:** A legitimate SASSA review SMS comes from a recognised registered short code (not a regular cellphone number or WhatsApp). It tells you to visit a SASSA office and lists the documents you need to bring. It does NOT contain a clickable link to "verify now" or ask for your banking PIN or card PIN.

**What a Genuine Review SMS Looks Like:** "SASSA: Your grant has been flagged for review. Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and proof of residence to complete the review. For enquiries call 0800 60 10 11." The message will be in plain text with no URLs, no payment demands, and no threats.

**Red Flags That Mean It Is a Scam:** The message asks you to click a link to "verify now", asks for your banking PIN or card PIN, demands payment to "process" the update, creates urgency ("update within 24 hours or your grant stops"), or comes from WhatsApp or a regular cellphone number.

**What If You Did Not Receive an SMS?** If you think you are due for a review but never received an SMS, it may be because your contact details are out of date. Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID to check your review status. Update your phone number if it has changed — see our guide on [changing your registered phone number](/guides/lost-phone-number).

**August 2026:** Beneficiaries flagged for grant review will receive an SMS from SASSA about their review appointment. These SMS messages asking you to visit a SASSA office are genuine — SASSA does not send review notifications via WhatsApp or social media. [Read the full announcement](/updates/update-2026-028).

Signs of a genuine SASSA request: the SMS comes from a recognised short code (not a regular cellphone number), the message tells you to visit a SASSA office (not a website link), the letter is on official SASSA letterhead with contact details, and the caller identifies themselves with their name and office location. If you are unsure, call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 to confirm before taking any action.
tips: SASSA will never ask for your PIN, OTP, or banking password — never give these to anyone.
If the message has spelling errors or comes from a WhatsApp number, it is almost certainly a scam.
When in doubt, call 0800 60 10 11 — do not use any phone number provided in the suspicious message.

steps.title: Step 2: Prepare Your Documents
steps.content: Once you have confirmed the request is genuine, gather the documents you need. The exact documents depend on why SASSA is asking you to update your information. General documents to bring: your original 13-digit South African ID book or Smart ID card (or alternative ID document if you use a permit), proof of residence (utility bill, bank statement, or lease agreement dated within 3 months), your SASSA card if you have one, and any documents that explain changes in your situation (e.g., marriage certificate if you changed your surname, proof of new income if you started working, death certificate of a spouse). Make photocopies of everything before you go.
tips: Call the SASSA office ahead of time to confirm which documents are needed for your specific update.
Keep your original documents in a separate bag from the copies — never hand over originals unless asked.

steps.title: Step 3: Visit the SASSA Office
steps.content: Go to your nearest SASSA office. Find the address and operating hours on our [SASSA offices page](/sassa-offices). Go early — offices open at 08:00 and queues form before then. When you arrive: take a queue ticket, wait for your number, explain to the officer that you are there to update your information (show them any SMS or letter you received), hand over your documents, answer any questions honestly, and ask for a confirmation slip or reference number when the update is complete. If the officer identifies additional documents needed, ask if you can bring them later the same day or if you need to make a new appointment.
tips: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday are generally less busy than Monday and Friday.
Bring water and a snack — wait times can be 2 to 3 hours at busy offices.

steps.title: Step 4: Confirm the Update Was Processed
steps.content: After your visit, the officer should confirm that your information has been updated in the system. Ask for the confirmation in writing or get a reference number. If SASSA said they would process the update and notify you, ask how long it will take — usually 3 to 7 working days for phone number changes, 1 to 2 working days for address or contact detail changes, and immediate for document verification updates. If you do not hear back within the stated timeframe, call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 and provide your reference number. Do not assume the update was processed if you did not receive confirmation.
tips: Write down the date, time, and name of the officer you spoke to.
Keep the confirmation slip with your other important documents.

steps.title: Step 5: Check Your Grant Status After the Update
steps.content: After your information has been updated, check your grant status to confirm everything is in order. For SRD grants, check online at srd.sassa.gov.za. For permanent grants, ask the SASSA officer to confirm your next payment date. If your grant was suspended pending the update, it should be reinstated within 7 to 14 working days. Check your status weekly after the update. If your grant has not been reinstated after 14 working days, call the SASSA helpline with your reference number.
tips: Check your status on the SRD portal between the 15th and 25th of the month for the most accurate result.
If your grant status shows 'Pending' for more than 30 days after the update, escalate to the SASSA helpline.

steps.title: Step 6: What If You Cannot Visit a SASSA Office?
steps.content: If you are too ill, disabled, elderly, or live too far from a SASSA office, you may qualify for a home visit or alternative arrangement. Call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 and explain your situation. SASSA may send an official to your home to verify your documents. This service is available for beneficiaries who cannot travel. Alternatively, you can authorise a trusted family member to attend on your behalf. You must give them a signed letter of authorisation, a copy of your ID, and the original documents they need to present. The family member must bring their own ID as well.
tips: Only trust a family member or close friend to handle your SASSA documents — not a stranger or 'agent.'
If you authorise someone else, give them a specific list of what to do and ask them to bring back a confirmation slip.

faqs.q: Is the SASSA SMS asking me to update my information real or a scam?
faqs.a: It depends. Genuine SASSA SMS messages come from registered short codes and ask you to visit a SASSA office. Fake SMS messages usually contain a link to click, ask for personal information, or demand payment. When in doubt, call 0800 60 10 11 to verify.

faqs.q: What does a genuine SASSA review SMS look like?
faqs.a: A genuine review SMS comes from a registered SASSA short code, tells you to visit a SASSA office with specific documents, and does NOT contain clickable links. It will never ask for your PIN or banking details. Example: 'SASSA: Your grant has been flagged for review. Visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and proof of residence. Call 0800 60 10 11 for enquiries.' Any message demanding immediate payment or asking you to click a link is a scam.

faqs.q: Can I update my SASSA information online instead of visiting an office?
faqs.a: Some updates can be done online. Phone number changes, banking details, and address updates may be done through the SASSA Self-Service Portal at www.sassa.gov.za. However, if SASSA specifically asked you to visit an office, you must go in person — the online portal may not allow the type of update needed.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore the request to update my information?
faqs.a: Your grant may be suspended until you respond. SASSA cannot continue paying a grant without accurate information on file. If your grant is suspended, it can be reinstated once you update your information, and you will receive back pay.

faqs.q: How long does it take for SASSA to process an information update?
faqs.a: Simple updates (address, contact details) take 1 to 2 working days. Phone number changes take 3 to 7 working days. Document verification updates are usually processed immediately during your office visit.

title: Best Bank Accounts for SASSA Beneficiaries in 2026: Low Fees & ATM Access Compared
description: Not all bank accounts are equal when you live on a SASSA grant. Compare Capitec, Postbank, TymeBank, FNB, Absa, Nedbank, Bank Zero, and Shoprite Money Market — monthly fees, ATM withdrawal costs, and hidden charges that eat into your grant.
imageAlt: Comparison of different bank cards on a table

steps.title: What to Look for in a SASSA-Friendly Bank Account
steps.content: When you live on a SASSA grant, every rand counts. An account charging R10/month in fees eats R120 from your grant every year. An ATM charging R8 per withdrawal adds up fast. Before choosing a bank account for your SASSA grant, check: the monthly account fee (must be R0), ATM withdrawal fees (free or cheap at the bank's own ATMs), branch access for cash deposits, eWallet and CashSend fees, and whether the bank allows a zero-balance account. The best account has zero monthly fees, free or cheap ATM withdrawals, and no minimum balance. 'Free' accounts often still charge for SMS notifications, other-bank ATM withdrawals, or paper statements — read the fine print.
tips: Open your SASSA-linked bank account in your own ID name — SASSA does not pay into third-party accounts.
Avoid accounts requiring a minimum monthly deposit — skipping a month triggers penalties.

steps.title: Postbank: The Official SASSA Bank (R0/month, Free ATM Withdrawals)
steps.content: Postbank issues the SASSA Black Card. Every SASSA beneficiary qualifies. Zero monthly fee. Three free withdrawals per month at any Postbank ATM. Additional withdrawals cost R2 to R8. Free balance checks via *120*3210#. The Black Card replaced the Gold Card in 2026. If you do not have a personal bank account, Postbank is the safest option — no fees, no minimum balance, and you can withdraw at any Post Office or retail store. The downside: Postbank's mobile app is basic and customer service can be slow. But for a no-frills account costing nothing, it is the best choice if you only need to receive and withdraw your grant.
tips: Postbank ATMs are free. Using a Capitec or FNB ATM costs R2 to R8.
Keep your PIN safe — Postbank has weaker fraud protection than commercial banks.

steps.title: Capitec Global One (R0/month, R7–R10 per Withdrawal)
steps.content: Capitec is the most popular bank among SASSA beneficiaries. The Global One account has no monthly fee if you do not swipe or use online banking in a month. You pay R7.50 per withdrawal at Capitec ATMs and R10 at other banks. The Capitec app is excellent — check balances, send money, buy airtime, lock your card. Capitec has branches in almost every town. The downside: Capitec charges R1 per SMS notification and R5 for a printed statement. If you withdraw R370 twice a month at a Capitec ATM, you pay R15 in fees — 4% of your grant. Still, Capitec is the best commercial option because of its app quality and wide branch network.
tips: Use the Capitec app to check your balance — this avoids the R1 SMS fee.
Capitec ATMs at Shoprite and Checkers are free — look for the Capitec logo before inserting your card.

steps.title: TymeBank (R0/month, R7/withdrawal, 4% Cashback)
steps.content: TymeBank is a digital bank with zero monthly fees. Open an account in 5 minutes using your ID number and cellphone — no branch visit. TymeBank charges R7 per withdrawal at Pick n Pay and Boxer kiosks. The big advantage: effective 4% cashback on your first R700 spend each month when you swipe at Pick n Pay, Boxer, or The Spaza Shop. For SASSA beneficiaries shopping at these stores, you get roughly R28 back on R370 spend. TymeBank also offers a savings pocket paying up to 11% interest. The downside: no physical branches — everything is done through the app or at Pick n Pay kiosks.
tips: Open your TymeBank account at any Pick n Pay or Boxer kiosk — takes 5 minutes.
Use your TymeBank card for all Pick n Pay purchases to earn the 4% cashback.

steps.title: Shoprite Money Market (Cash Collection, Not a Bank Account)
steps.content: The Shoprite Money Market is not a bank account. It lets you collect your SASSA grant in cash at any Shoprite, Checkers, or Usave till point. No account needed — bring your ID and SASSA card. No monthly fee, no ATM fee. Best for beneficiaries who do not have a bank account and prefer cash. The downside: collection during store hours only (08:00 to 20:00), queue at customer service, no online banking or deposits. For SRD beneficiaries receiving R370, it is practical if you live near a Shoprite.
tips: Avoid collecting in the first week of the month — queues are longest then.
Count your cash at the counter before walking away.

steps.title: FNB Easy, Absa Flexi, Nedbank Pay-as-Use Compared
steps.content: FNB Easy: R0/month, R10/withdrawal at FNB ATMs, R12 at other banks. Good app but higher fees than Capitec. Absa Flexi: R0/month, R10/withdrawal at Absa ATMs. Fewer rural branches. Nedbank Pay-as-Use: R0/month, R8/withdrawal at Nedbank ATMs. None match Capitec or TymeBank for low fees and rural accessibility. Bank Zero is new with R0 fees and R2 withdrawals at its own ATMs, but very few ATMs nationwide so far. For pure SASSA grant management, Capitec and TymeBank are the best value.
tips: Never use private ATMs at taxi ranks — some charge up to R15 per withdrawal.
Check your bank's ATM locator on their app before leaving home.

steps.title: Comparison Table: Best Bank Accounts for SASSA (2026)
steps.content:
Side-by-side summary:
Postbank Black Card — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: Free (3/month), R2–R8 after. Access: Post Offices nationwide. Best for: Free, no-frills banking.
Capitec Global One — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R7.50 (own ATM), R10 (other). Access: Excellent, most towns. Best for: Good app + wide branches.
TymeBank — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R7 (Pick n Pay/Boxer). Access: Pick n Pay stores only. Best for: Cashback on groceries.
Shoprite Money Market — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: Free at counter. Access: Shoprite/Checkers. Best for: Cash-only users near Shoprite.
FNB Easy — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R10. Access: Good in cities. Best for: Existing FNB customers.
Absa Flexi — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R10. Access: Moderate. Best for: Existing Absa customers.
Bank Zero — Fee: R0. Withdrawal: R2 (own ATM). Access: Limited. Best for: Tech-savvy urban users.
tips: Choose one bank and stick with it — multiple accounts mean more accounts for SASSA to scan.
If you switch banks, close your old account to reduce accounts linked to your ID.

faqs.q: Which bank is best for SASSA beneficiaries in rural areas?
faqs.a: Capitec has the widest rural branch network. Postbank is also widely available through Post Offices, but hours are shorter.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Postbank to Capitec for my SASSA payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Update your banking details on the SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za. The change takes effect the following month.

faqs.q: Does opening a second bank account affect my SRD grant?
faqs.a: Yes — SASSA scans all accounts linked to your ID. Stick to one account and keep it clean of non-grant deposits.

faqs.q: Are there truly free bank accounts in South Africa?
faqs.a: Postbank Black Card is the only fully free account. TymeBank and Capitec have no monthly fees but charge per ATM withdrawal.

title: Fix Missing SASSA Grant Payments
description: Your SASSA grant did not arrive? Learn why payments get delayed, how to check your status, and the exact steps to get your money back into your account.

steps.title: Wait 2–3 Business Days After the Official Payment Date
steps.content: Before you panic, check the calendar. Banks do not always process SASSA deposits on the same day. If your Pay Day was yesterday and the money is not in your account yet, wait at least 2 to 3 business days. This is especially true for standard bank accounts — Capitec and FNB often credit same-day, but Absa, Nedbank, Standard Bank, and smaller banks can take 1 to 3 days. Postbank Black Card credits are usually instant. If your status on the SRD portal says 'Approved' with a Pay Day, but you cannot see the money yet, wait the full 3 business days before taking further action. Check your [SASSA status online](/status-check) first to confirm the Pay Day.
tips: Capitec and FNB usually reflect payments within hours — if it has been 3 days with them, something is wrong.
SASSA payment dates are staggered — your neighbours may be paid on different days depending on grant type.

steps.title: Check Your SASSA Status Online — Is It Approved with a Pay Day?
steps.content: The single most important thing to check is your official SASSA status. Go to the [SASSA status check page](/status-check) and enter your 13-digit ID number. If your status shows 'Approved' with a specific Pay Day, the money has been allocated to you and the problem is likely a bank delay or incorrect banking details. If your status shows 'Pending' or 'Declined', the issue is with your application, not the payment. If it shows 'Referred' or 'Under Review', your grant is being reviewed — you may be scheduled for the Fourth Payment Day (see Step 4). Always check the official portal before calling anyone.
tips: Your online status is the source of truth — SMS notifications can be delayed or not sent at all.
If you cannot access the portal, use the SASSA USSD code *120*69277# to check from any phone.

steps.title: Verify Your Banking Details Are Correct and Your Account Is Active
steps.content: A very common cause of 'Approved but not paid' is incorrect or outdated banking details. Log into the SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za or the main SASSA website and review the bank account linked to your grant. Check: the bank name is correct, the account number has no missing or swapped digits, the branch code is correct, the account is open and active, and the account is registered in YOUR name — SASSA does not pay into third-party accounts. If the account was closed, frozen, or you changed banks and forgot to update SASSA, the payment will bounce back. Read our guide on [how to change your SASSA banking details](/guides/change-banking-details).
tips: Even one wrong digit in your account number will cause payment failure — re-type it carefully.
If you recently switched from a Gold Card to a Postbank Black Card, your banking details may have changed.

steps.title: Check If You Were Paid on the Fourth Payment Day (Grant Under Review)
steps.content: In August 2026, SASSA announced that beneficiaries flagged for review (due to the bulk means test or identity verification issues) would not be paid on the normal three-day payment cycle. Instead, they are paid on a special 'Fourth Payment Day'. For August 2026, that date is Friday, 07 August 2026. If your status shows 'Referred', 'Under Review', or if you received an SMS from SASSA asking you to visit an office, your payment may have been moved to the fourth day. Check the [SASSA Payment Calendar](/payment-calendar) for the exact fourth payment date each month. If you still have not been paid after the fourth payment day, you must visit a SASSA office with your ID to resolve the review status.
tips: Fourth payment day is typically the first Friday or Monday after the normal three-day cycle ends.
Being on fourth payment day means SASSA flagged your account — complete the review to return to normal payments.

steps.title: Check for SMS Notifications About Reviews or Life Certification
steps.content: SASSA frequently sends SMS messages to beneficiaries about outstanding actions. Check your phone's SMS inbox for messages from SASSA short codes. Look for: a request to complete life certification (also called eLife certification or annual verification), a request to visit a SASSA office for a review of your information, or a notice that your grant requires biometric verification. If SASSA sent you an SMS and you did not respond, your payment may have been held. Check our guides on [life certification](/guides/life-certification) and [biometric verification](/guides/biometric-verification-guide) for step-by-step help. If you lost the phone number registered with SASSA, you may have missed these SMS messages — follow our [lost phone number guide](/guides/lost-phone-number) to update it.
tips: SASSA sends multiple reminder SMS before holding a payment — check your spam or archived messages too.
If you changed your phone number, you will not receive SMS notifications until you update it with SASSA.

steps.title: Contact SASSA Toll-Free on 0800 60 10 11
steps.content: If you have checked all the above and your payment has still not arrived, call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11. The call is toll-free from any South African network. Before you call, get these ready: your 13-digit ID number, the phone number registered with SASSA, your banking details so they can verify what is on file, and the Pay Day date shown on your status. Explain clearly: 'My SASSA status says Approved with a Pay Day of [date], but the money has not reflected in my account.' The agent can check whether the payment was released, bounced back, or held for review. Ask for a reference number for your call. If the agent cannot resolve your issue, ask to speak to a supervisor or request an escalation.
tips: Call early in the morning (08:00) — afternoon wait times can exceed 30 minutes.
The helpline is open Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 16:00 — do not call on weekends.

steps.title: Visit Your Nearest SASSA Office as a Last Resort
steps.content: If you have tried all the steps above and still have not received your payment, visit your nearest SASSA office in person. Bring: your original South African ID book or Smart ID card, proof of residence (utility bill or bank statement), a printed copy of your SASSA status showing 'Approved' (if you can print one), and any SMS notifications from SASSA. Explain to the SASSA officer that you have not been paid despite an 'Approved' status. The officer will investigate and may process a manual payment or resolve the review flag on your account. This is a last resort — SASSA offices have long queues, so go early (before 08:00) and be prepared to wait. Find your nearest office on the [SASSA offices page](/sassa-offices).
tips: Bring water and a snack — queues at busy SASSA offices can take 2 to 3 hours.
If you are elderly or disabled, ask a trusted family member to accompany you or call 0800 60 10 11 to request a home visit.

faqs.q: How long should I wait before reporting a missing SASSA grant payment?
faqs.a: Wait at least 3 full business days after your official Pay Day. Banks process SASSA deposits at different speeds — Capitec and FNB are usually same-day, while other banks may take 1 to 3 days. If your status says 'Approved' but the money has not arrived after 3 business days, start investigating.

faqs.q: My SASSA status says 'Approved' but no money came — what's wrong?
faqs.a: This usually means one of three things: (1) A bank delay — wait 3 business days. (2) Incorrect or outdated banking details — check and update them on the SRD portal. (3) Your grant is under review and you have been moved to the Fourth Payment Day — check the SASSA Payment Calendar for the date.

faqs.q: My old age grant didn't arrive for 3 months — what should I do?
faqs.a: Three months of non-payment is serious and likely means your grant has been suspended. Common causes: you missed the annual life certification deadline, SASSA flagged you for a review you did not attend, or your banking details are incorrect. Call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 immediately and visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID. If your grant was suspended due to non-verification, complete the verification and you will receive back pay. See our guide on [how to reinstate a suspended grant](/guides/guide-reinstate-grant).

faqs.q: Can SASSA deduct money from my grant without telling me?
faqs.a: SASSA can deduct money from your grant only in specific circumstances and only with your written consent. Authorised deductions include: funeral policy premiums (if you signed up), loan repayments to SASSA-accredited lenders (if you took a loan against your grant), and medical aid contributions (if you opted in). SASSA cannot deduct money for unauthorised reasons. If you see unexpected deductions, call Postbank at 0800 53 54 55 to check if it is a card deduction, or call SASSA at 0800 60 10 11 to report unauthorised deductions.

title: SASSA Gold Card to Black Card Guide
description: The Gold Card stops working on 31 August 2026. Get your free Postbank Black Card at Shoprite, Checkers, or Pick n Pay. No fees, no forms, no queues.

steps.title: Deadline: 31 August 2026 — Gold Cards Will Stop Working
steps.content: The SASSA Gold Card will stop working after 31 August 2026. After this date, you will not be able to withdraw your grant payments, check your balance, or use the card at any retail store or ATM until you switch to the Postbank Black Card. Postbank has confirmed this is the final deadline — no further extensions will be granted. Around 2.9 million Gold Card holders need to make the switch. If you still have a Gold Card, act now to avoid losing access to your money.
tips: This is the fourth and final deadline set by Postbank — do not wait.
Help elderly or disabled family members switch before the deadline.

steps.title: Where to Get Your Postbank Black Card
steps.content: You can collect your free Postbank Black Card at any Postbank service point located inside these retail stores nationwide: Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer, and Spar. You do not need to go to a SASSA office for this — Postbank handles the card migration directly. There are hundreds of service points across all nine provinces, so there is likely one near you.
tips: Look for the Postbank desk inside the store — usually near customer services.
You can collect the card at any location in any province, not just where you registered.

steps.title: What to Bring — and It's FREE
steps.content: Bring your valid South African ID document (Smart ID card or green ID book). A temporary ID is also accepted. The entire process is FREE — there are no fees, no hidden charges, and no forms to fill in. The new Black Card is activated immediately when issued. Any money remaining on your old Gold Card transfers automatically to the new Black Card, so you will not lose any funds.
tips: You do not need proof of residence, bank statements, or any other documents.
If anyone asks you to pay for the card, report them immediately.

steps.title: How to Find Your Nearest Postbank Service Point
steps.content: To locate the closest Postbank service point, dial *120*355# from any cellphone. This USSD code is free and works on all South African networks (Vodacom, MTN, Cell C, Telkom). You will receive an SMS with the address of your nearest collection point. You can also call Postbank toll-free on 0800 53 54 55 for assistance.
tips: The USSD code *120*355# works on any phone — no internet needed.
Save the Postbank helpline 0800 53 54 55 in your phone contacts.

steps.title: Postbank Service Point Opening Hours
steps.content: Postbank service points operate during standard retail hours: Monday to Friday from 09:00 to 17:00. Some locations inside larger stores may also offer Saturday morning service, but this varies by store. It is best to visit during mid-week and mid-morning to avoid long queues. Avoid the last week of August when demand will be highest.
tips: Go on a Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday for the shortest queues.
Arrive early in the morning — service points get busy after 11:00.

steps.title: What Happens If You Miss the 31 August Deadline
steps.content: If you do not switch by 31 August 2026, your Gold Card will stop working completely. Your grant will still be paid into your Postbank account every month, but you will have no way to access the money until you get a Black Card. You will not be able to withdraw cash, buy goods, or check your balance. The only way to regain access is to visit a Postbank service point and collect your Black Card. Your money remains safe in your account — but it is locked until you make the switch.
tips: Do not wait until September — queues will be extremely long after the deadline.
Your grant payments accumulate in your account even if you cannot access them.

steps.title: Scam Warning: No Forms to Sign — Never Pay for Your Card
steps.content: Important: There are no forms for you to sign when collecting your Postbank Black Card. If anyone asks you to sign anything, it is a scam. The card replacement is completely free — no one should ask you for money. If someone demands payment, claims you need to 'activate' the card for a fee, or asks for your PIN or OTP, do not engage. Report them immediately to Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 or the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11.
tips: Postbank and SASSA will never call or SMS asking for your PIN or card details.
Destroy your old Gold Card yourself after receiving the Black Card.

steps.title: Black Card Works Immediately — Balance Transfers Automatically
steps.content: Your new Postbank Black Card works the moment you receive it. There is no waiting period or activation step. The full balance from your old Gold Card transfers automatically to the new Black Card — you do not need to do anything. You can start using the Black Card immediately at ATMs, retail stores, and any payment point in South Africa. Your grant payments will continue to be deposited into the same Postbank account as before.
tips: Test your Black Card at an ATM or retail store right after collecting it.
Your PIN remains the same as your old Gold Card PIN.

steps.title: Do NOT Go to SASSA Offices for Card Issues
steps.content: SASSA offices do not handle card replacements or card-related problems. The Postbank Black Card is managed entirely by Postbank. If you lose your card, it gets stolen, or you have any card-related issue, go directly to a Postbank service point or call the Postbank helpline on 0800 53 54 55. Going to a SASSA office for card issues will waste your time — they cannot help you with Postbank cards.
tips: SASSA handles grants; Postbank handles cards. Use the right channel.
For lost or stolen cards, call 0800 53 54 55 immediately to block the card.

faqs.q: Is the Gold Card to Black Card replacement free?
faqs.a: Yes, the replacement is completely free. There are no fees, no forms to pay for, and no hidden costs. If anyone asks you to pay for the card, it is a scam. Report them to Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 or the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't switch by 31 August?
faqs.a: After 31 August 2026, your Gold Card will stop working at ATMs, retail stores, and payment points. Your grant continues to be paid into your Postbank account, but you will not be able to access the money until you collect a Black Card from a Postbank service point. No further extensions will be granted.

faqs.q: Can I get a Black Card in any province?
faqs.a: Yes. You can collect your Postbank Black Card at any Postbank service point in any province — it does not have to be where you originally registered. Service points are located inside Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer, and Spar stores nationwide.

faqs.q: What if someone asks me to pay for the card?
faqs.a: Refuse and report them immediately. The Postbank Black Card replacement is free. No one from Postbank, SASSA, or any retail store should ask you for payment. Call Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 or the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11 to report the scam.

title: Grant Under Review? Fourth Payment Day
description: If SASSA paid you on a different day than other beneficiaries, your grant may be under review. Here is what you must do to get back on the normal cycle.

steps.title: What Is the Fourth Payment Day?
steps.content: SASSA normally pays social grants over three working days: Older Persons Grants first, then Disability Grants, then Children's Grants. A fourth payment day has been introduced for beneficiaries whose grants have been selected for review or eLife Certification. If you receive your grant on the fourth day, it means SASSA needs you to complete a grant review. This is not a penalty — it is a standard verification process required by the Social Assistance Act. You are still receiving your money; you just need to take an extra step afterward.
tips: The fourth payment day is always the day after Children's Grants are paid.
If you are unsure whether you were paid on the fourth day, check the date of your last deposit.

steps.title: August 2026 Fourth Payment Day Schedule
steps.content: For August 2026, the payment schedule is: Older Persons Grants on Tuesday 4 August, Disability Grants on Wednesday 5 August, Children's Grants on Thursday 6 August. The fourth payment day for beneficiaries under review is Friday 7 August 2026. If you do not receive your grant on the first three days and are under review, wait until Friday 7 August before contacting SASSA.
tips: Write down 7 August if you know you are under review — that is your pay day.
Do not queue at a SASSA office on 4, 5, or 6 August if your grant is under review.

steps.title: How Will You Know You Are Under Review?
steps.content: SASSA notifies beneficiaries selected for review via SMS before the payment cycle begins. The SMS explains that your grant has been flagged for review and that you will be paid on the fourth payment day. Check your phone messages carefully — the SMS may come from an official SASSA number. If you missed the SMS because your contact details are outdated, you will only discover you are under review when your payment does not arrive on the normal day.
tips: Keep your cellphone number and address updated with SASSA at all times.
If you changed your number recently, visit SASSA to update it immediately.

steps.title: What You Must Do After Receiving Payment
steps.content: Receiving your grant on the fourth payment day does NOT complete the review. You must visit your nearest SASSA office during the same month to complete the review process. Bring your original South African ID document. The SASSA officer will verify your details and confirm you still meet the eligibility criteria. After the review is complete, your grant will return to the normal three-day payment cycle from the following month.
tips: Go early in the morning (offices open at 08:00) to avoid long queues.
Complete the review within the same month — do not delay until the next payment cycle.

steps.title: What Happens If You Ignore the Review?
steps.content: If you receive your payment on the fourth day but do not visit a SASSA office to complete the review, your grant may be suspended during the next payment cycle. If your grant is suspended, you will not receive any payments until the review is completed. If you continue to ignore the review request, your grant may lapse entirely under the Social Assistance Act. A lapsed grant requires reapplying from scratch — your old application cannot be reinstated.
tips: A suspension can be reversed by completing the review, but a lapse cannot.
If you are bedridden or frail, contact SASSA about a home visit option.

steps.title: eLife Certification as an Alternative
steps.content: Some beneficiaries can complete the review process online through the SASSA eLife Certification portal instead of visiting an office. If you have a smartphone with a camera and internet access, you may receive an SMS link to complete your certification via facial recognition. However, many beneficiaries report that the eLife portal has technical problems — if the online method fails after several attempts, visit a SASSA office to complete the review in person.
tips: The eLife portal works best with good lighting and a stable internet connection.
Green ID book holders may struggle with facial recognition — visit an office instead.

steps.title: What Documents to Bring for the Review
steps.content: When visiting a SASSA office for your review, bring: your original 13-digit South African ID document (smart card or green ID book), proof of your current residence (utility bill or affidavit), proof of income if applicable (payslip or bank statements for the last 3 months), and any grant-specific documents (medical reports for disability grant, birth certificates for child support grant). Having all documents ready will ensure the review is completed in one visit.
tips: Make copies of all documents before going to the office.
Bring a pen — you may need to fill out forms at the office.

faqs.q: Why did I receive my grant on a different day than other beneficiaries?
faqs.a: You were likely selected for a grant review or eLife Certification. SASSA pays beneficiaries under review on a separate fourth payment day, which is always the day after Children's Grants are paid. Check for an SMS notification from SASSA confirming your review status.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't complete my grant review?
faqs.a: If you do not complete the review, your grant will be suspended in the next payment cycle. You will not receive payments until the review is done. Continued failure to respond may cause your grant to lapse, requiring a new application. Complete the review as soon as possible after receiving your fourth-day payment.

faqs.q: Can I complete the review online instead of visiting an office?
faqs.a: Some beneficiaries can use the eLife Certification portal to complete the review online via facial recognition. However, the portal has known technical issues. If the online method fails after several attempts, you must visit a SASSA office in person. Green ID book holders should plan to visit an office directly.

faqs.q: Will I need a review appointment even if I received my payment on the fourth day?
faqs.a: Yes. Receiving your payment on the fourth day does NOT complete the review. You must still visit a SASSA office to complete the review process. Once the review is complete, your grant will return to the normal three-day payment cycle from the following month. See our full guide on the [grant review and verification process](/guides/grant-verification-process) for what to expect at your appointment.

title: Fix SASSA eLife Certification Problems
description: eLife portal keeps loading? Facial recognition fails? OTP not received? This guide covers every known eLife Certification glitch and how to fix it.

steps.title: What Is eLife Certification and Why Is It Required?
steps.content: eLife Certification is SASSA's online identity verification system. It uses facial recognition technology to confirm that you are still alive and eligible to receive your grant. SASSA introduced it on 30 March 2026 as a digital alternative to in-person grant reviews. About 88% of users complete it successfully, but the remaining 12% experience problems. If you are among those who cannot complete it, this guide will help you troubleshoot.
tips: eLife Certification is required once every 12 months for most beneficiaries.
If the online method fails, you can still complete the review at a SASSA office.

steps.title: Problem: The Portal Keeps Loading and Never Opens Your Profile
steps.content: Many beneficiaries report that after entering their details, the system 'keeps loading and never goes through to my profile.' This is usually caused by high traffic, connectivity issues with the Department of Home Affairs interface, or using an outdated browser. Solution: Try accessing the portal during off-peak hours (early morning before 08:00 or after 18:00). Clear your browser cache and cookies. Try a different browser (Chrome or Edge work best). If using mobile data, switch to WiFi or vice versa.
tips: Peak hours are 09:00 to 15:00 on weekdays — avoid these times.
The portal works best on Google Chrome on a smartphone.

steps.title: Problem: Facial Recognition Fails After Multiple Attempts
steps.content: The most common complaint is facial recognition failing after 10, 20, or even 30 attempts. This happens because SASSA's system relies on the Department of Home Affairs database, which may have a low-quality photo (especially for green ID book holders). Solution: Ensure you are in a well-lit room with a plain background. Remove glasses, hats, and face coverings. Hold the phone steady at eye level. If you have a green ID book, the photo on Home Affairs' system may be too old — you will need to visit a SASSA office for fingerprint verification instead.
tips: Natural daylight works best — avoid harsh overhead lighting.
If you have a green ID book, go directly to a SASSA office rather than struggling online.

steps.title: Problem: OTP (One-Time PIN) Not Received or Marked as Wrong
steps.content: Some beneficiaries receive the OTP but the system says it is wrong. Others never receive the OTP at all. This is usually a network delay or a mismatch between the number you entered and the number registered with SASSA. Solution: Wait 10-15 minutes and request a new OTP — do not rush. Ensure you are entering the exact cellphone number registered with your SASSA application. If you changed your number, the OTP goes to your old number and you cannot access the portal.
tips: OTPs expire after 5 minutes — request a new one if time runs out.
If you changed your phone number, visit a SASSA office to update it first.

steps.title: Problem: 'Department of Home Affairs Not Available' Error
steps.content: This error means the SASSA system cannot connect to the Home Affairs database to verify your identity. It is not a problem with your details — it is a system error. Solution: Wait and try again later — the issue is usually temporary. If the error persists for more than 3 days, visit a SASSA office. SASSA has confirmed it is working on direct connectivity to DHA to reduce these interruptions, but the fix is still being implemented.
tips: This error is more common during weekends and public holidays.
SASSA staff can complete fingerprint verification even when the online system is down.

steps.title: Problem: You Never Received the Verification Link from SASSA
steps.content: Some beneficiaries say SASSA never sent the SMS with the verification link. This may be because your phone number is outdated, your SIM is not RICA-registered, or the SMS was blocked by your network. Solution: Check that your SIM is RICA-registered in your name. Ensure your phone number is the same one registered with SASSA. Contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 to request the link be resent. If the link never arrives, visit a SASSA office for in-person verification.
tips: Some networks block bulk SMS — ask your provider to unblock SASSA messages.
Until you complete verification, your grant status may show 'Self-Correction Required'.

steps.title: Final Option: Visit a SASSA Office for Fingerprint Verification
steps.content: If you have tried all troubleshooting steps and still cannot complete eLife Certification online, visit your nearest SASSA office. SASSA staff can complete fingerprint biometric verification, which is more reliable than facial recognition. According to SASSA's own data, there have been zero complaints about fingerprint verification, compared to 7,779 complaints about the facial recognition system. Bring your original South African ID document.
tips: Fingerprint verification is faster and more reliable — do not hesitate to use it.
Visit early in the morning (before 09:00) to avoid the longest queues.

faqs.q: Why does the eLife Certification portal keep failing?
faqs.a: The portal relies on the Department of Home Affairs database, which can experience connectivity issues. Other causes include high traffic during peak hours, outdated browser, or a poor-quality photo on the Home Affairs system (common for green ID book holders). Try during off-peak hours, clear your cache, and use a different browser.

faqs.q: I tried facial recognition 20 times and it still failed — what now?
faqs.a: Visit your nearest SASSA office for fingerprint verification. SASSA has confirmed fingerprint verification has zero reported complaints compared to 7,779 for facial recognition. It is the more reliable method. Bring your original South African ID document.

faqs.q: How long does eLife Certification take to process?
faqs.a: Once you successfully complete the facial recognition, the verification is processed immediately. Your grant status updates within 24 hours. If you complete fingerprint verification at a SASSA office, the update is also immediate.

title: SASSA Grant Deductions Explained
description: Money missing from your SASSA grant? Learn about loan repayments, funeral policies, and other deductions — and how to stop unauthorised ones.

steps.title: Common Types of SASSA Grant Deductions
steps.content: SASSA deducts money from grants for several legitimate reasons. The most common deductions are: loan repayments to SASSA-accredited micro-lenders (if you took a loan against your grant), funeral policy premiums (if you signed up for a policy linked to your grant), electricity prepaid vouchers (in some municipal areas), school feeding scheme contributions (in certain provinces), and administration fees for payment collection at certain retail points. Not all deductions apply to every beneficiary, and some are optional.
tips: You have the right to know what is being deducted and why.
Most deductions require your written consent before they can be applied.

steps.title: How to Check What Is Being Deducted
steps.content: If you see money missing from your grant, you can check the reason in several ways. Call the SASSA toll-free helpline on 0800 60 10 11 and ask for a breakdown of deductions. Visit your nearest SASSA office and request a payment history printout. Check your SMS notifications — SASSA sometimes sends details of deductions by SMS. Check your bank statement for the name of the organisation receiving the deduction. If a deduction is active that you did not authorise, you have the right to dispute it.
tips: Keep your SMS and bank statements as evidence of deductions.
Ask for a transaction history report at any SASSA office.

steps.title: Loan Deductions from SASSA-Accredited Lenders
steps.content: If you took a loan from a SASSA-accredited micro-lender (such as Mzansi Loans, JUMEME, or similar lenders), the lender may deduct repayments directly from your grant. These deductions are legal but regulated. The maximum amount that can be deducted is 33.3% of your grant. You have the right to cancel the debit order directly with the lender or through SASSA. If deductions continue after the loan is fully repaid, contact SASSA immediately.
tips: Never give your SASSA card or PIN to a lender as 'security' for a loan.
If a lender takes more than 33.3% of your grant, report them to SASSA.

steps.title: Funeral Policy Deductions
steps.content: Some funeral insurance companies partner with SASSA to deduct premiums directly from beneficiary grants. If you signed up for a funeral policy and agreed to premium deductions, you will see monthly deductions on your grant payment day. These deductions must be authorised by you in writing. If you no longer want the policy, contact the insurer directly to cancel. If deductions continue after cancellation, report it to SASSA.
tips: Read the terms of any funeral policy carefully before signing.
You can have multiple deductions stopped by visiting a SASSA office.

steps.title: What to Do If a Deduction Is Wrong or Unauthorised
steps.content: If you believe a deduction is incorrect, unauthorised, or continuing after it should have stopped: first, check your grant payment history at a SASSA office to identify exactly which organisation is making the deduction. Second, contact the organisation directly and request a refund. Third, if they do not resolve the issue, contact the SASSA fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11. Fourth, if the deduction is causing financial hardship, request a suspension of all deductions at your nearest SASSA office. SASSA can stop all third-party deductions from your grant if you demonstrate hardship.
tips: Do not ignore deductions — the longer they continue, the more money you lose.
If an unauthorised deduction persists, lodge a formal complaint with SASSA.

steps.title: Can You Opt Out of All Deductions?
steps.content: Yes, in most cases you can opt out of voluntary deductions. Loan repayments can only be stopped once the loan is fully repaid. Funeral policy deductions can be cancelled by contacting the insurer. Electricity and school feeding deductions require you to contact your municipality or school to opt out. If you are experiencing financial hardship, visit a SASSA office and request a 'deduction suspension' — SASSA has the authority to pause most third-party deductions temporarily.
tips: SASSA cannot stop deductions for debt repayments ordered by a court.
Request everything in writing and keep copies of all correspondence.

faqs.q: Why is money being deducted from my SASSA grant?
faqs.a: Money may be deducted for loan repayments, funeral policy premiums, electricity prepaid vouchers, or school feeding contributions. Most deductions require your written consent. Check your payment history at a SASSA office to see exactly what is being deducted and by whom.

faqs.q: Can I stop deductions from my SASSA grant?
faqs.a: Yes, for most voluntary deductions. Contact the organisation making the deduction (loan provider, insurer, municipality) and request cancellation. If they do not stop, visit a SASSA office and request a deduction suspension. Loan repayments cannot be stopped until the loan is fully repaid.

faqs.q: How do I check what is being deducted from my grant?
faqs.a: Call SASSA on 0800 60 10 11, visit a SASSA office for a payment history printout, or check your bank statement for the name of the organisation receiving the deduction.
